name: IPC-2014 (International Planning Competition 2014) evaluation suite
description: This article reviews the 2014 International Planning Competition (IPC‐2014), the eighth in a series of competitions starting in 1998. IPC‐2014 was held in three separate parts to assess the state of the art in three prominent areas of planning research: the deterministic (classical) part (IPCD), the learning part (IPCL), and the probabilistic part (IPPC). Each part evaluated planning systems in ways that pushed the edge of existing planner performance by introducing new challenges, novel tasks, or both. The competition surpassed again the number of competitors that participated in its predecessor, highlighting the competition's central role in shaping the landscape of ongoing developments in evaluating planning systems.
evaluation_method: coverage (number of problems solved), plan quality/cost, and runtime; competition scoring typically combines solved-instance counts with plan quality
general_score_metric: coverage (solved instances) combined with plan quality (domain-specific scoring used in IPC)
notes: Multi-track, domain-dependent benchmark for classical/learning/probabilistic planners; not an LLM benchmark; results strongly depend on domain modeling and planner heuristics; older but widely cited in planning research.
